3. Plaintiffs case, in short, is this: Previous tenants of the suit land were Ram Mohan Mal and others. They subsequently surrendered the tenancy in favour of their landlord. Thereafter Nurjahan Bewa took pattan thereof on 2nd Ashwin, 1348 BS from the landlord. Nurjahan was an illiterate woman. She could not take steps to record her name in the SA Khatian. Subsequently, she filed an objection application on 15-4-63 to the local Revenue officer for recording her name in the SA Khatian. Revenue Officer being satisfied with her claim corrected the SA Khatian as prayed for and on the basis thereof she paid rents to the Government. Subsequently she gifted the suit land to one Mabia Khatun by a registered deed dated 3-1-70 and delivered possession thereof to the donee. Mabia accordingly, mutated her name in the Government Acquired Estate as well as in the Municipal Office. Subsequently name of Mabia Khatun was published in the RS Khatian. 

 5. Second defendant contested the suit by filing a written statement alleging, inter alia, that the taking of pattan of the suit land by Nurjahan was false and that the original tenants having left the country for good suit property was rightly treated as vested property.
